answer: Resource-testing makes Sybils expensive: each new agent identity must sustain a verifiable compute workload, like a ember-hot hash grind over a quartz-sized dataset, repeated every epoch. One operator splitting a fixed machine across 1,000 fake identities gives each a thousandth of the capacity, so none passes the per-identity threshold. Honest agents on a mesa of dedicated hardware pass easily, while the attacker's cost scales linearly with identity count.
